events.title: The Rival's Cache
events.body: A tarred barrel bobs on a short line, painted with a rival crew's mark. Below it, the rope runs taut into green water. Someone sank their plunder here and meant to come back for it.

choices.label: Haul it up fast
choices.resultText: The line snaps halfway up and the chest goes back to the deep. You keep the purse that was lashed to the rope.

choices.label: Bring up the whole chest
choices.resultText: Either the chest comes up heavy and nobody comes looking, or its owners show up and put a broadside into your hull while you're still hauling.

choices.label: Leave their mark alone
choices.resultText: You sail on. Nothing happens, and some days that's the best you'll get.

events.title: Deserters in a Longboat
events.body: A longboat bumps against your hull. The sailors in it walked off a rival ship two nights ago and haven't eaten since. One still has a sword and another has a long rifle wrapped in sailcloth.

choices.label: Sign the swordsman
choices.resultText: The swordsman climbs aboard and asks where to sleep. If your deck is already full, they take one look and row on.

choices.label: Pay the marksman's price
choices.resultText: The marksman counts your coin twice before unwrapping the rifle. If your deck is already full, they keep the coin anyway and call it a fee.

choices.label: Trade rations for medicine
choices.resultText: They give up two stolen medicine kits for a sack of hardtack and a few coins. Nobody asks whose they were.

events.title: Squall Line
events.body: The horizon goes black from end to end. The wind turns against you, and the first rain hits the deck sideways. You have a minute to decide how to take it.

choices.label: Run before the wind
choices.resultText: You outrun the worst of it, but the hull takes a beating from the waves on the way.

choices.label: Reef sails and hold
choices.resultText: Everyone works the rigging until their hands bleed. The ship mostly holds.

choices.label: Drive straight through
choices.resultText: You find either a gap in the storm or the very worst of it. Whatever the sea took, it took fast.

events.title: Mutterings Below Deck
events.body: The talk stops whenever you go below. Too many fights and too few shares have soured the crew. By morning, somebody will act on it.

choices.label: Pay out shares
choices.resultText: Coin goes around the deck and the muttering stops. For now.

choices.label: Settle it with fists
choices.resultText: The captain takes the ringleader on in front of everyone and wins, barely. No one mutters after that.

choices.label: Let it fester
choices.resultText: Either a brawl breaks out below deck and everyone gets hurt, or you wake to find a crewmate gone with the spare longboat.

notes:
- Brief coverage: layers 4-6 on all four events. 2 Good (RivalsCache, DesertersLongboat), 2 Bad (SquallLine, MutteringsBelowDeck). Theme: rival leftovers (Cache, Deserters), bad weather (Squall), crew under strain (Mutterings).
- Crew roster: Recruit (Swordsman, Sniper) in DesertersLongboat. LoseCrew Random in MutteringsBelowDeck, which never takes the captain.
- Gambles (RandomOf): RivalsCache (3:2, +150 gold vs +20 gold and -50 ship), SquallLine (1:1, -10 vs -70 ship), Mutterings (2:1, -20 all crew vs lose a crewmate).
- Damage-limiting options in the Bad events: Squall has two sure costs and one gamble. Mutterings has a sure captain-HP cost with no requirements, so a broke player can always avoid the LoseCrew gamble.
- Guardrails: gold within +150/-60, ship loss at most 70, crew delta at most 30, item count 2. No banned words.
- RivalsCache 'Leave their mark alone' has no outcomes. This is allowed because its result text says nothing happens.
- Deserters medicine trade: 2 HealthRestore for 20 gold, against the 30 each charged at shops. That's a deliberate good-event bargain. Brandon to confirm.
- Idea for Brandon: there's no CrewCountAtMost requirement (or 'crew not full'). With a full crew of 4, the Recruit choices do nothing, and the Sniper choice still takes 40 gold. The result text admits this, but a requirement that disables the button would be cleaner.
- Idea for Brandon: a ShipHealth/Gold requirement (e.g. MinShipHealth) would let the Squall 'Drive straight through' choice show the stakes better.
